messages:
Sam: Quick heads-up — we've been seeing short bursts of exporter retries when telemetry-ingest has brief GC/scale blips. Proposing a per-trace + per-exporter 'retry budget' and some dampening so we don't thrash the ingest layer. Thoughts?
Anya: +1. Pure exponential backoff still lets a lot through when many clients retry simultaneously. A budget/token-bucket per trace_id or per-exporter instance makes sense.
Mike: Is the budget the same across OTLP protocols? gRPC streams behave differently than HTTP/protobuf (stream vs unary). For gRPC we can delay/hedge, for HTTP maybe drop earlier.
Lee: Also important: idempotency trade-offs. OTLP duplicates are tolerable but increase storage/ingest cost. We should differentiate retry behavior for traces vs metrics/legacy logs.
Zara: I'd prefer policy rules: 429 -> client backoff with increasing penalty, 5xx -> fast circuit open on exporter instance, network timeouts -> retry budget consumption. Also keep a short global cooldown on repeated fails. :thinking_face: 
Sam: Agree. Practical config sketch (prototype):
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp/primary:
    endpoint: telemetry-ingest.redwood.internal:4317
    protocol: grpc
    tls: true
    timeout: 10s
    retry:
      enabled: true
      initial_interval: 200ms
      max_interval: 2s
      max_elapsed_time: 20s
      strategy: budgeted
      budget:
        per_trace: 3    # max retries allowed for a given trace_id across exporters
        instance_rate: 50/min  # token refill per exporter instance
      dampening:
        window: 30s   # after N drops, reduce retry rate for 30s
```
Anya: Love the per_trace cap. Implementation note: we need the collector/agent to carry trace_id through retry bookkeeping. Might be tricky for batching where many trace_ids in one batch — token accounting must be per-span-set.
Mike: For batching/size behavior, consider "span-size shedding" — if batch is too big and backend rejects due to payload, drop largest spans first (or split) instead of full retry. That reduces work and keeps tail latency down.
Lee: Metrics we should emit: `telemetry.retry_budget.used`, `telemetry.retry_budget.dropped`, `telemetry.exporter.circuit_state`, and per-protocol `telemetry.otlp.grpc.active_streams`. Then surface them in Console with a per-route alert.
Zara: UX ask: in Console rollout UI, show a small "telemetry health" row with retry budget burn rate and exporter error % so PD/resilience teams can correlate with app incidents.
Sam: Ops/alerts: alert if `telemetry.retry_budget.dropped > 10% for 5m` or if exporter circuit is open for >1m. Also add a runbook note: if backpressure persists, scale ingest or divert non-critical routes to SLO-relaxed ingest.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Telemetry exporter v2.1.3 rollout started to staging (canary=2 nodes).
Anya: I'll prototype the collector-level budget and expose the metrics. Will push a small config flag behind `--feature-budgeted-retries`.
Mike: I'll add the Console tiles and make an alert playbook. We should iterate after 1 day of canary. :thumbsup:
Sam: Perfect — thanks team. If we see weird edge cases (batches with mixed trace_ids) let's reconvene and maybe handle accounting at batch split time.
